bull_bear.body:
- First Indian MSO to launch GPON FTTH, with 6.3 million home passes and approximately 91,000 kilometres of fibre optic cable covering pan-India
- Subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited, providing group backing
- Cable business consistently secures a top-two market position in key urban centres, with presence in all major metros and mini-metros across over 700 towns
- Availability of unlimited data across all broadband plans is described as a key differentiator
- Service quality edge: Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) score of 96%, 87% of non-network customer issues resolved within one hour, and a 72% same-day activation rate positioning the Company among the fastest broadband installers in the industry
- AI-driven automation across customer support plus re-engineered engagement platforms (live chat/live call transfer, digitised activation, time-slot appointment scheduling) reducing activation TAT by almost 3 hours
- Established infrastructure, wide geographic presence and strong LCO partnerships underpinning the cable distribution business
- Owns both broadband and cable distribution, enabling hybrid OTT-cable and bundled offerings
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Broadband subscriber attrition — The wireline broadband base declined to 1.02 million subscribers as on March 31, 2026 from 1.06 million a year earlier, so growth depends on ARPU and customer-quality improvement rather than volume.
- Cable television reach depends on fellow subsidiaries and joint ventures — Hathway Digital serviced approximately 4.63 million viewers as on March 31, 2026 'including through fellow subsidiaries and joint ventures', so a material part of the cable footprint sits outside the directly held entity; a restructuring exercise to simplify the group structure was undertaken during the year.
- Persistent uncertainty in the external / global environment — FY26 was an unusually challenging year on the external front with heightened trade uncertainty and penal tariffs; FY27 is expected to be a year of adjustment and the external environment remains uncertain, shaping the overall outlook.
- Downside-dominated global growth and protracted trade conflicts — The medium-term global outlook is described as dim with downside risks dominating; a protraction of trade conflicts would weigh on investment and further weaken global growth.
- AI-driven asset valuation correction — If the AI boom fails to deliver the anticipated productivity gains, it could trigger a correction in overly optimistic asset valuations with potential for broader financial contagion.
- Energy security shock and stagflation risk — The 2026 US-Iran conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, affecting roughly 20% of global oil and LNG supplies, are driving surging energy and fertilizer costs, raising stagflation risk and cutting 2026 global growth forecasts, with India among the economies heavily dependent on Middle Eastern supply.
- Trade and capital-flow volatility transmitting to India — Slower growth in key trading partners, tariff-induced disruptions to trade and volatility in capital flows could intermittently weigh on exports and investor sentiment, though these are characterised as manageable external uncertainties rather than immediate macroeconomic stress.
- Inflation measurement and re-firming — Inflation has moderated to historically low levels but some firming is expected going forward, and the forthcoming rebasing of the CPI series will have implications for inflation assessment, warranting careful interpretation of price dynamics.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Hathway provides fixed line services through ISP and CATV to homes across pan-India, and is one of the leading fixed line internet service providers in the country, offering high-speed connectivity along with OTT offerings. It was the first Indian MSO to launch GPON FTTH and has 6.3 million home passes, a 1.02 million broadband subscriber base and approximately 91,000 kilometres of fibre optic cable. Its wholly owned subsidiary Hathway Digital Limited is one of India's largest Multi System Operators, running 2 main head-end facilities with 4 re-transmission centres over approximately 41,000 kilometres of fibre optic cable, serving cable subscribers across over 700 towns and adjoining areas; the Company also delivers CATV and broadband in certain parts of the country through its associate company GTPL Hathway Limited.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Broadband (ISP):** GPON FTTH high-speed home broadband with unlimited data across all plans, Dual-band Optical Network Units (ONUs) / dual-band routers with Wi-Fi band-steering technology, OTT offerings bundled with broadband, AI-enabled WhatsApp chatbot self-service and digitised sales/activation platforms
- **Cable Television (Hathway Digital Limited):** Standard Definition (SD) digital cable television services, High-Definition (HD) digital cable television services, Owned channels / own platform services, Digital Video Broadcasting over Cable (DVB-C) services, Customer-curated channel packages under the New Tariff Order (NTO) framework

outlook.body: - The Board reviews annual operating plans, capital deployment strategies and budget evaluations as a standing part of its agenda, alongside periodic assessment of key business risks and mitigation measures. Governance of distributions and group structure is codified in Board-approved policies published on the Company's website - a Dividend Distribution Policy, a Policy for determining Material Subsidiaries, a Related Party Transactions Policy (with a policy on materiality of RPTs and material modifications), a Policy on determination and disclosure of Materiality of Events and a Vigil Mechanism and Whistle-blower Policy. The Board has a Risk Management Committee and an Audit Committee in place with compliance confirmed under Regulations 17 to 27 of the Listing Regulations, and a risk assessment and risk management plan is placed before the Board.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Hathway's expansion is network-led rather than plant-led, and no rupee capex programme or dated project is disclosed in the routed text. On the broadband side the Company continued to strengthen its business through the deployment of advanced Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) technology supported by digitization and automation initiatives that enhanced network performance and customer experience, enabling 4K and 8K video streaming, online gaming and video conferencing; it was the first Indian MSO to launch GPON FTTH and now has 6.3 million home passes, approximately 91,000 kilometres of fibre optic cable and 1.02 million subscribers as on March 31, 2026. During the year it introduced industry-first dual-band Optical Network Units (ONUs) with integrated Wi-Fi band-steering technology and standardized dual-band routers across high-speed plans, lifting average speed 6% from 105 Mbps in Q4 FY25 to 111 Mbps in Q4 FY26, and undertook proactive network improvement that cut network-related complaints 28%. On the cable side, Hathway Digital Limited operates 2 main head-end facilities with 4 re-transmission centres over an optical fibre network spanning approximately 41,000 kilometres, serving more than 700 towns and adjoining areas. Looking ahead, the Company states it will continue to invest in network modernization, AI-led customer experience and digital platforms to strengthen its competitive positioning and capitalize on growing demand for high-speed reliable broadband.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Economic Survey 2025-26 projects India's real GDP growth in FY27 in the range of 6.8% to 7.2%, with FY27 expected to be a year of adjustment as domestic demand and investment gain strength.
- India's medium-term growth potential is assessed to have been lifted closer to 7% by the cumulative impact of policy reforms, with domestic drivers dominant and the balance of risks around growth broadly even.
- The Indian M&E sector grew 9.1% in 2025 to reach Rs 2.78 trillion; it is expected to grow 2.8% in 2026 to Rs 2.86 trillion, and excluding online gaming to grow 8% in 2026 and then at over 7% CAGR to Rs 3.3 trillion by 2028 (EY estimates).
- Digital media is expected to grow at a 14% CAGR to Rs 1,640 billion (Rs 1.64 trillion) by 2028, making it the single largest absolute growth contributor in the M&E sector.
- Linear TV revenues are expected to decline at 5% until 2028, with advertising falling at 7% and subscription falling at 3% - a structural headwind for cable distribution.
- Television households are expected to cross 200 million by 2028 and Indian households to rise from 332 million in 2025 to 345 million by 2028, supporting demand for TV sets.
- Connected TV homes are expected to increase to 67 million by 2028 as home broadband access increases to over 90 million homes by 2028; India's wired broadband base rose from 32 million to 46 million over the last two years.
- Bundled offerings are expected to accelerate as DPOs counter cord cutting by integrating Pay TV content with IPTV and broadband services.
- Growth for linear TV is expected to come from TV-dark households and rural markets via conversion of Free-to-Air viewers into lower-priced 'Pay-TV Lite' packs and reactivation of dormant set-top boxes, while urban markets grapple with subscription fatigue.
- Advertising grew 13.5% in 2025, faster than the sector, on e-commerce and point-of-sale advertising and improved MSME credit; digital advertising at 63% of total advertising dominated marketing budgets.
- Global growth is projected to remain resilient at 3.3% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 with headline inflation declining to 3.8% in 2026, but the medium-term global outlook remains dim with downside risks dominating.
- Key global watch-items flagged: an AI boom that fails to deliver productivity gains could correct asset valuations, and a protraction of trade conflicts would weigh on investment; the 2026 US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz blockade are driving an energy security crisis and stagflation risk.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Hathway Cable and Datacom Limited, a subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited, is a pan-India fixed-line services provider delivering FTTH broadband through its ISP business and digital cable television through its wholly owned subsidiary Hathway Digital Limited.

open.item: Under the TRAI Seventh Amendment Regulations effective April 1, 2026, the Company as a distributor must conduct annual financial-year audits of its addressable systems and submit the audit report to broadcasters by 30th September each year.

The Company will continue to invest in network modernization, AI-led customer experience and digital platforms to strengthen its competitive positioning and capitalize on growing demand for high-speed broadband.
Despite a marginal decline in the broadband subscriber base, the Company remains focused on improving customer quality, driving ARPU growth and enhancing customer lifetime value.

The cable business intends to sustain and grow its subscriber base through the rollout of next-generation set-top boxes, hybrid OTT-cable offerings and ongoing network upgrades, leveraging established infrastructure and LCO partnerships.

The Company will continue proactive engagement with TRAI, MIB and industry stakeholders on regulatory matters, particularly the overhaul of the current regulatory regime and audit framework implementation under the Seventh Amendment.

Management flagged continued decline in cable television subscriber numbers and sustained structural headwinds on the traditional cable distribution model from OTT proliferation and changing consumer preferences.
The annual report presents, as its future outlook, that digital revenue will grow at a 14% CAGR to reach Rs 1,640 billion by 2028 (EY estimates).
Linear TV revenues are projected to decline at 5% until 2028, with advertising falling at 7% and subscription falling at 3% - a trackable headwind for the Company's cable television business.

Connected TV homes are expected to increase to 67 million by 2028 as home broadband access increases to over 90 million homes by 2028, expanding the addressable market for the Company's wireline broadband business.

The Company continued to strengthen its broadband business through deployment of advanced Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) technology supported by digitization and automation initiatives that enhanced network performance and customer experience.
